summary: # Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video: Dress Making ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will explore the process of modifying a T-shirt into a dress, focusing specifically on creating a pleated top. This video will guide you through the steps necessary to achieve a well-structured design using Marvelous Designer. ## Step 1: Setting Up the Layers We begin by working on the outer layer of the puller sound effect. Select the inner layer of the clothing panel, then copy and paste one layer. Move this layer to the inner layer near the 3D window. ### Reason for Layer Choice The reason we don't use the column layer here is that it will automatically exist. ## Step 2: Adjusting the Layers Next, delete any unnecessary lines and activate the outer layer panel. Move the elements to the inner layer, ensuring that there is no overlapping. Use the line powder tool to mix the upper and lower layers of the clothing's inside and outside together. ### Mixing the Sleeves The sleeves should also be mixed together. Operate on the back in the same way. ## Step 3: Further Modifications After removing the needle, use the free powder tool. Press the same must-adhere sleeve and outer layer panels. Select the free powder tool and first create a seam line part of the shoulder. ### Aligning the Panels Press SHIFT to re-match the front and back of the phone in the same direction of volume, then loosen the SHIFT key to complete the creation. ## Step 4: Simulation and Stability Open the simulation to examine the穿着性 (wearability). After assessing the wearability, activate all of the lining panels to maintain overall stability. ### Waistband Simulation Next, simulate the waistband. You will notice two folds in the front; this is due to the deletion of the rope, but the sewing line between the ropes remains. Use the editor sewing line tool to delete these lines. ## Step 5: Checking the Chest Area At this point, check the chest area. You may find that the board is bent because the type of sewing line is set to Custom Angle, causing the seam to bulge at the edge. Change this to Turned to flatten the seam. ### Modifying Folds Make necessary adjustments to the folding positions, such as the hem and back of the upper eye. If the chest is not smooth, you can modify the position of the seam line using the methods shown in previous videos. ## Step 6: Freezing and Fabric Application Select the inner layer of the board and freeze them. Then select the outer layer of these boards and apply the fabric for the sleeves and skirt. ### Addressing Folds After changing the fabric, you may notice some folds. Select the front and middle lines, and during the movement, press the Shift key to level them out. This stretching will create folds without affecting the sleeves. ## Step 7: Detailed Fold Adjustments Lower the outer layer of the chest to see more detailed fold effects. Press the Shift key to move them to the level. Activate the inner layer of the board and modify it together. Use the Ctrl key to adjust the levels as well. ### Shortening and Merging Shorten the line in the front to flatten the bulge in that area. After shortening, merge the front and back pieces by pressing Ctrl C to move the edges. ## Step 8: Dealing with Holes After merging, if you notice holes in the 3D window, address any unstable areas promptly. Repeat the same steps for the back and center. If the drag is not effective, pause the simulation, pull out the sheet first, then simulate again. ## Step 9: Adjusting Particle Strength Reduce the particle strength to enhance the distribution of the fold. Manually drag the sheet to adjust the fold distribution, then reduce the particle strength to 5 and repeat the adjustments. ### Increasing Folds Fewer folds at the seam area can be modified by adjusting the physical properties of the fabric. Copy the existing fabric and reduce the particle strength to 0. ## Step 10: Transparency Display After adjustments, turn on the transparency display. You will find that there is more volume at the waist, which can be adjusted through rules. Set the shrink rate to negative to shrink the part of the grid. ### Final Adjustments On the panel, click and drag the mouse. As the blue area deepens, the fabric will shrink after simulation. ## Step 11: Refining the Back Piece The corner on the side of the back piece may be too sharp. After sewing, this could lead to protrusions. Slightly adjust it to maintain a smooth rhythm. ### Simulation Review After simulation, confirm that the waist does not appear too pronounced and is more suitable for the model. ## Step 12: Creating the Pattern Now, let's create the pattern for the outer circle of the costume. First, select the line of the inner layer of the costume and the sleeve part, then check the total length. ### Rectangular Tool Usage Select the rectangular tool to create a rectangle with twice the width and a height of 15 mm. This will create a rectangular pattern. ## Step 13: Applying the Line Powder Tool Use the line powder tool by first clicking on the edge of the flower, then pressing the Shift key. In the same direction, click on the front, sleeve, and back pieces. ### Final Adjustments Select these two flower edges, and in the menu at the right-hand corner, select the side of the addition. This addition will be arranged on the side of the top and sleeve. ## Conclusion Cool the back piece to prevent instability, activate the simulation, and ensure all panels are simulated together to guarantee stability. Adjust any elements as necessary to achieve your desired design outcome.
